Chapter 9: Leaving a Legacy—Impacting the Next Generation
As the years go by, have you ever wondered what you'll leave behind? When the work is done, the kids have grown, and the spotlight has faded, what really remains? For a lot of us, there's this deep-down desire to leave something lasting—a mark on the world, or maybe just a quiet gift to those who come after.
I’m reminded of a grandfather who, looking back over his life, realized that his greatest influence had nothing to do with his career or any awards he’d won. Instead, it was found in the simple, everyday moments with his grandkids. Reading stories together, sharing meals, passing on wisdom, and sharing laughter. Those memories stuck around long after the toys were packed away and the house grew quiet.
Most of us don’t realize just how much our everyday choices shape the future. How a man treats his spouse, the words he speaks to his children, even the small priorities he sets—every single one of these leaves a mark. Legacy isn’t built in one big moment. It’s the result of lots of small, faithful acts, day after day.
Think about the story of a teacher who, year after year, invested in his students. He wasn’t the flashiest or the most popular, but he listened. He encouraged. He saw potential in each kid. Decades later, students would come back—not to thank him for what he taught, but for how he made them feel seen and valued.
It’s easy to fall into the trap of thinking legacy is all about big achievements or public recognition. But honestly, someone chasing after God’s heart learns that the most lasting impact usually happens in hidden places—through simple acts of kindness, steady faithfulness, and genuine love.
Mentoring is such a powerful way to invest in the next generation. Picture a man, getting close to retirement, who starts meeting regularly with a younger colleague. They talk about everything—work, family, faith, even failure. That friendship becomes a well of wisdom and encouragement for both of them. And it’s in those moments you realize: legacy isn’t just about what you leave behind. It’s about who you help along the way.
So, if you’re thinking about legacy, here’s an invitation—be intentional. Invest in relationships. Share your story, your struggles, your faith. The seeds you plant today? They might just bear fruit for generations to come.
